[[File:Kronprins Gustaf Adolf hedersdoktor Chicago.jpg|thumb|Crown Prince [[Gustaf VI Adolf of Sweden|Gustaf Adolf]] of Sweden receives his doctor's diploma as an honorary doctorate from the University of Chicago from the university's president, Professor Max Mason, 1926]]
'''Charles Max Mason''' (26 October 1877&ndash;22 March 1961), better known as '''Max Mason''', was an American mathematician. He served the [[President of the University of Chicago|4th president]] of the [[University of Chicago]] from 1925 to 1928 and as the third president of the [[Rockefeller Foundation]] from 1929 to 1936.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=May 1961 |title=Max Mason |journal=[[Physics Today]] |volume=14 |issue=5 |page=76 |doi=10.1063/1.3057580 |language=en|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Weaver |first=Warren |date=1964 |title=Max Mason 1877{{ndash}}1961 |url=https://www.nasonline.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/mason-max.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181022232538/http://www.nasonline.org/publications/biographical-memoirs/memoir-pdfs/mason-max.pdf |archive-date=2018-10-22 |access-date=2017-09-13 |website=[[National Academy of Sciences]] |language=en}}</ref>

Mason's mathematical research interests included [[differential equations]], the [[calculus of variations]], and electromagnetic theory.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=O'Connor |first1=J. J. |last2=Robertson |first2=E. F. |date=August 2005 |title=Max Mason (1877 - 1961) - Biography - MacTutor History of Mathematics |url=http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Mason.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220121181806/https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Mason/ |archive-date=2022-01-21 |access-date=2022-03-21 |website=[[University of St Andrews]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Education==
*B.Litt., 1898, [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]]
*Ph.D., Mathematics, [[University of Göttingen]], 1903.
**Dissertation: "Randwertaufgaben bei gewöhnlichen Differentialgleichungen" ([[Boundary value]] functions with ordinary differential equations)
**Advisor: [[David Hilbert|Hilbert]]

==Career==
* [[MIT|Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT), 1903–1904, Instructor of Mathematics.
* [[Yale University]], 1904–1908, Assistant Professor of Mathematics.
* [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], 1908–1909, University of Wisconsin–Madison, Associate Professor of Mathematics.
* University of Wisconsin–Madison, 1909–1925, Professor of [[Physics]].
**[[United States National Research Council|National Research Council]], 1917–1919, Submarine Committee. (Invented a [[submarine]] detection device, which was the basis for [[sonar]] detectors used in [[World War II]].)
* University of Chicago, 1925–1928, President.
* Rockefeller Foundation, 1928–1929, Director, Natural Sciences Division.
* Rockefeller Foundation, 1929–1936, President.
* [[Palomar Observatory]] (California), 1936–1949, Chairman of the team directing the construction of the observatory.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1948-06-04 |title=Vast Hope in 'Big Eye' |volume=111 |page=6 |work=[[The Kansas City Star|The Morning Kansas City Star]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |issue=134 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/653546327 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2022-03-21 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |language=en}}</ref>

On 2 May 1945, he appeared on [[Edgar Bergen]]'s radio show to chat about the new observatory and trade jokes with [[Charlie McCarthy]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=1948-04-25 |title=Radio This Week |volume=68 |page=11D |work=[[The Kansas City Star]] |issue=221 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/655792380/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=2022-03-21 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |language=en}}</ref> In 1948, he, along with [[Lee Alvin DuBridge|Lee A. DuBridge]], [[William Alfred Fowler|William A. Fowler]], [[Linus Pauling]], and [[Bruce Hornbrook Sage|Bruce H. Sage]], was awarded the [[Medal for Merit]] by President [[Harry S. Truman]].<ref name="Pauling">{{Cite web |title=Presidential Medal for Merit. February 2, 1948. - Published Papers and Official Documents - Linus Pauling and the International Peace Movement |url=http://scarc.library.oregonstate.edu/coll/pauling/peace/papers/1948h.1.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180718074029/http://scarc.library.oregonstate.edu/coll/pauling/peace/papers/1948h.1.html |archive-date=2018-07-18 |access-date=2022-02-26 |website=[[Oregon State University]] |language=en}}</ref>
